tier_reason: The rurban/smhasher README table and the linked table.html list wyhash 22640.53, xxh3 20853.74, City64 14390.09 and Murmur3A 3027.30 MiB/sec, and doc/wyhash.txt matches. The suite code is public and the CPU is named (Ryzen 5 3350G), but no compiler or flags are given, so B (well-known independent suite) and not A.

corrections.workload: SMHasher bulk speed test: average MiB/sec across alignments 0-7 when hashing 262144-byte keys, plus small-key (1-31 byte) cycles/hash, on the suite's default reference machine.
corrections.hardware: Default reference machine: AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz per the smhasher README (table.html says 'AMD Ryzen 5 PRO 3350G 3.6GHz workstation'); compiler/flags not stated
corrections.caveats: wyhash's own README/repo has no benchmark table (only benchmark.cpp). The numeric win over xxHash comes from the independent rurban/smhasher shootout, which names the CPU (AMD Ryzen 5 3350G) but not the compiler or flags, so this is capped at Tier B. The margin over xxh3 is narrow (~9%) and depends on workload and CPU; other CPUs in the suite's linked tables may reorder the two. The wyhash README itself says wyhash 'has evolved into rapidhash', its faster successor. The Unlicense is OSI-approved but has no explicit patent grant.

notes: All four numbers match the correct rows on the smhasher README and table.html. Metadata checked: Unlicense, 1148 stars, last commit 2026-03-23, not archived or forked. The usage claims (Zig, V, Nim, Go 1.17, abseil, Windows Terminal) come from the wyhash README.

tier_reason: The fmtlib/dtoa-benchmark README table shows dragonbox 28.95 ns, to_chars 51.35 ns and sprintf 744.72 ns (25.723x) on an Apple M1 Pro with Apple clang 21.0.0. The benchmark code is public (src/benchmark.cc, src/dragonbox-test.cc, src/to_chars-test.cc), and CMakeLists.txt pins CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (CMake's -O3 -DNDEBUG), so the flags come from the committed build config.
notes: The 1.77x ratio (51.35/28.95) is correctly derived. The license (Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR BSL-1.0) matches the README and the LICENSE-Apache2-LLVM and LICENSE-Boost files; the gh spdx value of 'Apache-2.0' is incomplete. The last default-branch commit is 2025-09-12, just over 12 months ago, so 'stale' is correct. The A tier relies on the flags being fixed by the build type in the public CMakeLists.txt, not printed next to the results.

tier_reason: The arXiv paper (published in SPE 51(8), 2021) compares against glibc strtod in Section 12. Its setup names GCC 10.2 with -O3 -DNDEBUG, and Table 8 lists the CPUs (i7-6700, EPYC 7262, Ampere Skylark, POWER9). The benchmark code is public at lemire/simple_fastfloat_benchmark (tag v0.1.0 exists). Table 9 shows Skylake canada at 45 vs 9.0 Mfloat/s.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: GNU GCC 10.2, -O3 -DNDEBUG, single-threaded, in a privileged Ubuntu 20.10 Docker container on Linux (main Table 9); also MSVC 19.26.28806 /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG (Table 13) and Apple clang 12.0.0 -O3 -DNDEBUG (Fig. 3)
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed paper (Daniel Lemire, Software: Practice and Experience 51(8), 2021). Benchmark code: github.com/lemire/simple_fastfloat_benchmark (git tag v0.1.0). The main Linux comparison is against glibc strtod, because GCC/libstdc++ had no float std::from_chars at the time. The paper also tests Visual Studio 2019's std::from_chars (MSVC STL) and strtod on an Intel 7700K (Table 13, canada: 37 vs 6.7 Mfloat/s for from_chars, ~5.5x, derived from page data), plus Apple's strtod on an M1 (Fig. 3). libc++ from_chars was not tested. Ratios vary by dataset: the integer dataset shows smaller wins (e.g. 61 vs 20 Mfloat/s on Skylake).

notes: The Section 12 quote and the Table 9 Skylake canada numbers (45 vs 9.0) are verbatim in the paper. The existing caveat wrongly said MSVC STL was not tested, because Table 13 does test it. The license is triple (Apache/MIT/Boost) per the README and LICENSE-* files, not only Apache-2.0. Metadata checked: 2114 stars, last commit 2026-09-23, active.

tier_reason: The fmtlib/dtoa-benchmark README table shows ryu 46.07 ns against sprintf 744.72 ns (16.164x), and to_chars 51.35 ns, on an Apple M1 Pro with Apple clang 21.0.0. The code is public (src/ryu-test.cc, src/sprintf-test.cc), and CMakeLists.txt pins the Release build type (-O3 -DNDEBUG).

corrections.caveats: Ryu's own README gives Ryu Printf speedups against platform printf of 15x (glibc), 4x (musl), 9x (MSVC), 8-20x (msys) and 24x (Apple libc). It names no CPU, only OS/libc versions, so that first-party claim alone is Tier C. This record cites the independent fmtlib/dtoa-benchmark (compiler and CPU stated), which shows a 16.164x win over C sprintf for shortest d2s. Against std::to_chars (libc++), the margin is only ~1.11x (46.07 vs 51.35 ns, derived from page data). The results are a single hardware sample (Apple M1 Pro), and the Release build config comes from CMakeLists.txt. Licensing: all code is Apache-2.0, and files in ryu/ may also be used under BSL-1.0.

notes: The existing caveat overstated the Ryu README range as 15x-24x; the README table actually runs from 4x (musl) to 24x. The benchmark calls d2s_buffered_n (the README method table says d2s_buffered). Metadata checked: 1354 stars, last commit 2026-02-09, gh spdx Apache-2.0.

tier_reason: The fmtlib/dtoa-benchmark README table shows fmt 36.84 ns against sprintf 744.72 ns (20.214x) and ostringstream 885.30 ns, on an Apple M1 Pro with Apple clang 21.0.0. The code is public (src/fmt-test.cc uses FMT_COMPILE), and CMakeLists.txt pins the Release build type (-O3 -DNDEBUG).
